title: The ten, closed
hook: ten perfections, ten great lives, ten days of living them
tomorrow: can cutting mats or stocking shelves be practice?

segments.voice: Yesterday: Narada's equanimity. Calm helps, because a soft answer leaves room to turn around. That was the last of the perfections. Today they all come back at once.

Packing for a trip with one carry-on teaches you fast what you actually use. Today the perfections go into one bag, and the question is which one goes on top. Which do you need most right now? The tradition's quiet answer: the one your week keeps asking for. A week of short tempers asks for patience. A week of putting things off asks for resolve. A week of feeling invisible might ask for kindness, starting with yourself.
screen: `ONE CARRY-ON.` → `WHICH GOES ON TOP?` → `THE ONE YOUR WEEK ASKS FOR.`

segments.voice: Here are the ten, each with the great life that, tradition says, shows it. Generosity: Vessantara. Virtue: Bhuridatta, the naga prince who kept his precepts when captured. Renunciation: Temiya, the silent prince. Wisdom: Mahosadha. Effort: Mahajanaka, swimming with no shore in sight. Patience: Candakumara. Truth: Vidhura. Resolve: Nemi. Kindness: Sama, kind even to the king who shot him. And equanimity: Narada, calm with a king who'd lost his way. That's the Theravada list, set out in texts like the Buddhavamsa; Mahayana texts count the perfections their own way. Each one is a parami: a perfection, a quality brought to fullness. And look at the shape. Not ten trophies on a shelf, but ten strengths the Bodhisatta built across many lives, one hard situation at a time. They lean on each other. Truth needs resolve. Kindness without wisdom can go soft; equanimity without kindness can go cold. So you don't pick one and drop the rest. You pick the one that's next. And next doesn't have to be grand. Patience with one coworker counts. Truth in one message counts.
screen: `TEN QUALITIES, TEN GREAT LIVES.` · `THE THERAVADA LIST.` · `BUILT ONE HARD SITUATION AT A TIME.` · `THEY LEAN ON EACH OTHER.` · then, large: `TEN PERFECTIONS.`

segments.voice: Hold up both hands. Touch one fingertip for each perfection as you say it under your breath: generosity, virtue, renunciation, wisdom, effort, patience, truth, resolve, kindness, equanimity. Go round once more, slower, and notice which finger you'd like to stay on.
The ten: the paramis, the perfections, from generosity to equanimity, each told through one of the Bodhisatta's great lives.
Your line: ten perfections, and one of them is next for you. Thirty of thirty, and the ten are closed.
